author: Airielle Lowe
description: Vivek Ramaswamy, who was endorsed by President Donald Trump, is projected to win the Republican primary for governor in Ohio, according to NBC.
title: Ramaswamy Wins Republican Governor Primary in Ohio, NBC Projects

author: Mark Niquette
description: Voters in Ohio handily backed former presidential candidate Vivek Ramaswamy’s bid to be the Republican nominee for governor, while Democrat Sherrod Brown will get another shot at returning to the Senate after being defeated in 2024.
title: Trump Ally Ramaswamy, Democrat Brown Win Primaries in Ohio

author: Catherine Lucey, Daniel Carvalho, Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump will host Brazilian counterpart Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva Thursday, amid tensions over the Iran war and its impact on the global economy.
title: Trump to Meet With Brazil’s Lula Thursday for Economic Talks

author: Abhishek Vishnoi
description: Narendra Modi’s party’s historic West Bengal win tightens his national grip after a 2024 setback, with analysts saying the result may spur infrastructure spending and boost industrial stocks in a market lacking clear catalysts.
title: Modi Win Boosts India’s Industrial Stocks in Catalyst-Dry Market

author: Jennifer A Dlouhy
description: President Donald Trump said he would pause a US-led effort to help stranded ships exit the Strait of Hormuz to see if an agreement with Iran to end the war could be finalized.
title: Trump Says US to Pause Guiding Ships While Seeking Iran Deal

description: Representative Bryan Steil (R-WI), Chair of the House Administration Committee and member of the House Financial Services Committee, says while he hopes to see lower interest rates in the near future, the Fed must remain "data-driven, not politically-driven" in its decision making. He highlights the inflationary impact of elevated energy prices, saying supply constraints tied to tensions in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz are driving costs higher, while expressing hope a resolution with Iran will help "unlock" oil flows. He also expresses optimism Congress can pass stablecoin legislation as soon as July to boost consumer protection and US competitiveness, and backs increased security funding for the president amid rising threats. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power: Late Edition," live from The Milken Institute Global Conference in Beverly Hills, California. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Rep. Steil: Fed Must Be 'Data-Driven, Not Political'

description: Javier Garcia, CEO of World Central Kitchen, discusses the humanitarian impact of the conflict in the Middle East, saying he hopes to provide meals in Iran “if we can,” while noting the group would need to partner locally to operate there. He details ongoing efforts in Gaza—where the organization has served up to one million meals a day—and Ukraine, emphasizing its model of “going in, training, and building capacity” with local communities. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power: Late Edition," live from the Milken Institute Global Conference in Beverly Hills, California. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: World Central Kitchen CEO: Will Aid Iran 'If We Can'

author: Jen Judson
description: The US Army on Tuesday shot a Tomahawk missile from its Typhon Mid-Range Capability launcher system in the Philippines during a military exercise, marking the first time it has fired such a weapon since the system’s arrival in the country two years ago, which drew a rebuke from China.
title: US Army Fires First Tomahawk From Philippines in Exercise

description: Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) expresses optimism about the path forward for the CLARITY Act in Congress. She also discusses the future of AI regulation, the outlook for Democrats in the 2026 Midterms, and ongoing operations in the Strait of Hormuz, saying that she's hopeful her Republican colleagues will try to hold the administration accountable. She speaks with Kailey Leinz on Bloomberg's "Balance of Power," joining from Solana Accelerate, Solana’s flagship US event in Miami. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Sen. Gillibrand on CLARITY Act Timeline

author: Eric Martin, Josh Wingrove, Eltaf Najafizada
description: The US said offensive operations against Iran are over as it shifts to protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, but the targeting of another cargo vessel after a day of strikes signaled that the conflict is dragging on.
title: US Says Offensive Phase of Iran War Over as Ship Hit in Strait

author: David Alire Garcia
description: Trump is pursuing "American dominance" in the region with the biggest-ever buildup of US troops.
title: The US Is Flexing Its Military Might in Panama – And Keeping Latin America On Edge

author: Eric Martin
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he expects President Donald Trump and Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping to discuss Taiwan when they meet next week and that neither nation wants to destabilize the Indo-Pacific region.
title: Rubio Says Neither US, China Want Asia Destabilized Over Taiwan

description: Rick Rieder, BlackRock global fixed income chief investment officer, talks about how the Federal Reserve could operate under Kevin Warsh, managing geopolitical risk and the future of the yield curve. He speaks to Bloomberg Television at the Milken Global Conference.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: BlackRock's Rieder Sees 10-Year Yield Dropping to 4%

author: Nancy Cook
description: Republican dominance in the state is under threat in the midterm election campaign.
title: Iowa Returns to its Battleground Status for the Midterm Elections

author: Courtney McBride
description: The State Department has approved Ukraine’s request to purchase up to $374 million worth of GPS-guided bomb kits, according to an announcement Tuesday.
title: US Approves $374 Million Sale of Guided Bomb Kits For Ukraine

author: Arne Delfs
description: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz ruled out the possibility of forming a minority government amid a possible breakup of his current two-party coalition, which has slid into a crisis only a year after taking power.
title: Merz Rules Out Minority Government, Election as Coalition Stalls

description: Pfizer Inc. Chief Executive Officer Albert Bourla says President Donald Trump's nominee to lead the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention is a good choice. Bourla says Erica Schwartz is a “very credible scientist." Bourla also talks about earnings, their drug pipeline and doing business in China. He speaks to Bloomberg's David Westin. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Pfizer CEO on Drug Pipeline, Trump's Pick to Lead CDC

description: After 25 years, American soldiers are back in Panama to train in the jungle alongside local forces. It's part of President Donald Trump's aggressive push to secure "American dominance" in the region. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Why US Troops Are Training in Panama

author: Josh Wingrove
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio said his upcoming trip to Rome and the Vatican was planned before President Donald Trump got into a spat with Pope Leo XIV, characterizing the visit as part of regular engagement with the Holy See.
title: Rubio Says His Trip to Vatican Was Planned Before Trump Dustup

description: Bridgit Mendler, Northwood founder and CEO, said that her company is aimed at creating communications networking infrastructure for the whole space industry, so that companies aiming to get to space can spend less time and money on communications and more time on innovation.  Mendler said that the world is opening up its excitement around space innovation and that the Artemis NASA mission proved that similar missions can be possible on a mainstream level. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Artemis II Proved That Space Innovation Is Possible In Mainstream, Says Bridgit Mendler

description: Citadel founder Ken Griffin says it's clear that New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani doesn't welcome success because he wants to put special taxes on billionaires. Griffin spoke Tuesday during an interview at the Milken Global Conference. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Griffin Says NYC's Mamdani Doesn't Welcome Success

author: Eric Martin, Josh Wingrove
description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio emphasized that the move to give military support to ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz near Iran is a “defensive operation,” saying the US will only fire if fired upon.
title: Rubio Says US Operation in Hormuz Strait Is Defensive in Nature

description: On the early edition of Balance of Power,  Bloomberg's Joe Mathieu and Carol Massar discuss how industry is searching for answers to affordability crises as war impacts critical supply chains. On today's show, president and CEO of the Center for American Progress Neera Tanden, Free Russia Foundation Vice President Vladimir Kara-Murza, chief at Zelle Denise Leonhard, CEO of Nuclear Energy Institute Maria Korsnick,  US Chamber of Commerce president Suzanne Clark, and Northwood founder and CEO Bridgit Mendler.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Industry Leaders Look for Energy Solutions at Milken | Balance of Power: Early Edition 5/5/2026

description: Citadel founder Ken Griffin says New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has proven that he made the right choice in moving from Chicago to Miami. “What the mayor of New York has made clear to my partners, and principally my New York partners, is that we need to double down on our bet in Miami," Griffin said during an interview at the Milken Global Conference. He also wouldn't say if he's going to finish building a new tower in Manhattan at 350 Park Avenue. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Griffin Says Mamdani Made It Clear That He Needs to Double Down on Miami

author: Greg Stohr, Justin Wise, Jordan Fischer
description: Tensions are starting to boil over at the US Supreme Court.
title: Supreme Court Sniping Heats Up as Justices Near Opinion Season

description: Vladimir Kara-Murza, vice president of the Free Russia Foundation, said as long as Russia remains a dictatorship under Vladimir Putin it will be a threat to Europe and the rest of the world. Kara-Murza said that the 'sympathies' of the Trump White House are with Putin, despite the President's claims that he is keeping pressure on Putin to end the war in Ukraine. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Administration 'Sympathies' Are With Putin, Says Kara-Murza

author: Magdalena Del Valle
description: The US and its allies are pushing a draft United Nations Security Council resolution that would open the door to sanctions or even military action if Iran doesn’t ease its chokehold over the Strait of Hormuz.
title: US Seeks Support Via the UN to Break Iran’s Hormuz Chokehold

author: Nicolle Yapur, Vinicius Andrade
description: The US government authorized Venezuela to hire advisers for potential debt talks, a key step in the long-awaited path to restructure the country’s $60-billion pile of defaulted bonds. The notes soared after the announcement.
title: US Authorizes Venezuela to Hire Advisers for Debt Talks

author: Katherine Burton
description: Ken Griffin said he plans to make Citadel’s Miami tower even bigger after New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani name-checked the billionaire in his pledge to charge taxes on second homes.
title: Griffin Says He’s Doubling Down on Miami Amid Mamdani Feud

author: Myles Miller, Alicia A. Caldwell
description: New York’s push to limit state cooperation with federal immigration authorities will trigger a surge in enforcement activity, with more agents deployed into communities and an increase in arrests beyond initial targets, said White House border czar Tom Homan.
title: Border Czar Sees New York ICE Surge as Hochul Pushes Cooperation Curbs

description: Former Middle East Senior Advisor to President Biden Amos Hochstein joins Bloomberg at the Milken Institute Global Conference to discuss the war in Iran. He says we're going towards a cliff on oil and oil products by the end of this month and that the bite will deepen every day. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: We're Going Towards a Cliff on Oil Says Hochstein

author: Jen Judson
description: Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is assembling top defense contractors as well as Palantir Technologies Inc. and Anduril Industries Inc. in a bid to get their weapons to communicate better with each other and to more closely integrate AI.
title: US Army Wants Its Weapons Systems to Talk to Each Other

description: President Donald Trump says the US has "total control" of the Strait of Hormuz and Iran wants to make a deal to end the war. He speaks in the Oval Office. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump Says US Has 'Total Control' Over Hormuz Strait

author: Julian Lee, Alex Longley
description: No region of the world produces more oil and gas than the countries straddling the Persian Gulf. Most of this energy can only be exported aboard tankers that cross the Strait of Hormuz — a waterway that’s effectively been blocked for more than two months.
title: How the Strait of Hormuz Has Become a Weapon of War

description: US companies could choose to report earnings semiannually instead of quarterly under a proposal released by the Securities and Exchange Commission. Bloomberg Intelligence's Nathan Dean has more on "Bloomberg Crypto." (Source: Bloomberg)
title: SEC Unveils Proposal for Semiannual Reporting

author: Jorge Valero
description: The European Union wants the main parts of a US trade deal adopted by July, as it pushed Washington to respect previous commitments made under the pact.
title: EU Tells US Trade Deal Should be Adopted by July Deadline

author: Josh Wingrove
description: US President Donald Trump said he would discuss the Iran war with Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping during their summit next week and sought to downplay tensions over the conflict.
title: Trump Says Xi Has Been ‘Respectful’ on Iran, Downplaying Strains

author: Lydia Beyoud
description: US companies could choose to report earnings semiannually instead of quarterly under a proposal released by the Securities and Exchange Commission, potentially reducing how much information publicly-traded firms must share with investors.
title: SEC Unveils Plan to Let Companies Move to Semiannual Reports

author: Allyson Versprille
description: The Trump administration is proposing rules to tighten security against rogue drone flights.
title: FAA Proposes Limits on Drone Flights to Address Security Worries

author: Shruti Srivastava, Siddhi Nayak
description: India’s federal cabinet on Tuesday approved a credit guarantee plan with capital allocation of 181 billion rupees ($1.9 billion) to help businesses and airlines cushion the impact of the war in Iran.
title: India Clears Loan Guarantee Plan as War Hurts Firms, Airlines

author: Dale Crofts
description: A Moscow court ordered the nationalization of billionaire Vadim Moshkovich’s stake in agricultural business Ros Agro Plc after prosecutors filed an anti-corruption lawsuit against him, according to local media outlet RBC.
title: Russia Court Orders State Seizure of Agriculture Tycoon’s Empire, RBC Says

author: Brian Platt
description: Prime Minister Mark Carney has appointed Louise Arbour, a former Supreme Court judge who held several top roles at the United Nations, as Canada’s next governor general.
title: Carney Appoints Former Supreme Court Judge Louise Arbour as Governor General

author: Chris Strohm, Michael Smith
description: Shortly after ascending to the top of the Justice Department last month, Todd Blanche gathered prosecutors in Miami to press for results from a highly sensitive probe into some of President Donald Trump’s perceived political enemies.
title: A Probe of Trump Foes Upends Justice Department Hub in Miami

author: Sara Munoz
description: Vornado Realty Trust Chief Executive Officer Steven Roth said he’s begging Zohran Mamdani to be more welcoming to businesses after a video by the New York City mayor caused Citadel to threaten to pull out of a new tower on Park Avenue.
title: Vornado CEO Appeals to Mamdani After Mayor’s Griffin ‘Blunder’

author: Henrique Almeida
description: Portuguese Finance Minister Joaquim Miranda Sarmento said his government plans to move ahead with a proposal to impose a tax on energy companies’ windfall profits, drawing on measures used during the 2022 fuel price crisis.
title: Portugal Set to Propose New Windfall Tax on Energy Firms

author: Francois de Beaupuy, William Horobin
description: France announced fresh measures to curb reliance on Chinese rare earths in a move to safeguard industries ranging from consumer electronics to electric cars and offshore wind.
title: France Unveils Rules to Reduce Reliance on China for Rare Earths

author: Julian Lee
description: Value of shipments hit the highest since the conflict began on higher flows, prices
title: Russia Boosts Oil Exports as Value Spikes to Ukraine-War High

author: Catherine Lucey
description: President Donald Trump is slated to sign a memorandum Tuesday that brings back the Presidential Fitness Test Award, according to a White House official, part of a broader effort by the administration to revamp US public health policies.
title: Trump to Sign Memo Bringing Back Presidential Fitness Test

description:
US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said the US will maintain its “ironclad” blockade of Iranian ships in the Strait of Hormuz during a press briefing at the Pentagon.  The US played down the prospect of a return to active war with Iran after a day of clashes involving ships in the Strait of Hormuz and missile strikes against the United Arab Emirates.
Attacks by Tehran on vessels in the Persian Gulf and the UAE didn’t constitute a breach of a ceasefire, General Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, told reporters at the Pentagon on Tuesday. Speaking alongside him, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth confirmed the truce that began just under a month ago is still in place.  (Source: Bloomberg)
title: The Ceasefire is Not Over With Iran Says Hegseth

author: Jim Wyss
description: Trading of Canada’s Goldquest Mining Corp is scheduled to resume Tuesday after the Dominican Republic halted development of its Romero gold mine project in the wake of mass protests.
title: Dominican Republic Protests Derail Canadian Gold Mining Project

author: Alex Morales, Tom Rees
description: Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves enjoys a “good relationship” with her US counterpart Scott Bessent, a spokesman for the UK government said following a Financial Times report that the two finance ministers argued in Washington last month.
title: Reeves Enjoys Good Ties With Bessent, UK Says After Clash Over Iran

description: US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth said the US will maintain its “ironclad” blockade of Iranian ships in the Strait of Hormuz during a press briefing at the Pentagon. He tells US allies and the rest of the world that “Project Freedom” to guide ships through the strait is a temporary mission and “at the appropriate time and soon, we will hand responsibility back to you.” (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hegseth Says US Is Stabilizing Hormuz, But the World Needs to Step Up Soon

description: Speakers participate in a panel discussion during the Milken Institute Global Conference in Beverly Hills, California. Photographer: Lauren Justice/Bloomberg
title: Updates From Milken Institute Global Conference

author: S'thembile Cele, Ntando Thukwana
description: South Africa’s foreign ministry is stepping up diplomatic efforts to quell growing concern on the continent about rising anti-immigrant sentiment in the country.
title: South Africa Moves to Quell Fallout From Anti-Immigrant Attacks

author: David Herbling
description: Kenya’s government plans to introduce tax measures to help raise nearly $1 billion, risking a return to protests stoked by similar proposals two years ago.
title: Kenya Risks Return to Deadly Protests With $1 Billion Tax Plan

author: Maya Averbuch, Michael D McDonald
description: La lotería oficial del país enfrenta a nuevos rivales online y también a versiones ilegales que llevan años vendiéndose en las calles. Organizaciones de beneficencia terminan perdiendo.
title: Una lotería ilegal se ha convertido en un dolor de cabeza para Costa Rica

author: Maya Averbuch, Michael D McDonald
description: Nimble new rivals are threatening official sweepstakes, and charities are losing out.
title: Illegal Lotteries Are Beating Governments at Their Own Game

author: Joe Lovinger
description: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton held a slim edge over incumbent John Cornyn in a new poll as the state’s bitter Republican Senate primary nears its finale.
title: Ken Paxton Narrowly Leads John Cornyn in Bruising Texas GOP Race

author: Maggie Eastland, Shirin Ghaffary
description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Microsoft Corp. and xAI have agreed to give the US government early access to their artificial intelligence models to assess the systems’ capabilities and help improve their security before the technology is released to the public.
title: AI Firms Agree to Give US Early Access to Evaluate Their Models

author: Andra Timu, Irina Vilcu
description: Romania’s minority government collapsed after losing a no-confidence vote, throwing the country into renewed political turmoil and potentially stalling reforms needed to narrow the widest budget shortfall in the European Union.
title: Romanian Government Falls, Sowing Doubts Over Fiscal Reforms

author: Jonathan Tamari
description: Elections this month will test the president’s power within the GOP in his second term
title: Trump’s Political Revenge Tour Launches in Three States

author: Enda Curran
description: Elizabeth Warren pressed Stanley Druckenmiller’s investment firm to free Federal Reserve chair nominee Kevin Warsh from confidentiality agreements, seeking greater transparency into his investments before a Senate confirmation vote.
title: Warren Asks Druckenmiller to Reveal Details on Warsh Investments

author: Josh Xiao
description: Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is traveling to Beijing for talks, marking the diplomat’s first visit to China since US and Israeli strikes sparked the most severe global oil supply shock in history.
title: Iran Foreign Minister Heads to China for First Time Since War

author: Cliff Harvey Venzon, Neil Jerome Morales
description: Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told visiting Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi that their countries, both US treaty allies, will need to deepen cooperation in Asia even as Washington focuses much of its attention on the Middle East.
title: Philippines to Deepen Japan Ties While US Focuses on Iran

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Cash is making a comeback in Russia as digital payments grow more unreliable with frequent mobile internet outages the Kremlin says are aimed at countering the threat of Ukrainian drone attacks.
title: Russians Turn to Cash as Internet Blackouts Undo Digital Economy

author: Andras Gergely
description: Hungary’s incoming Prime Minister Peter Magyar accused his predecessor Viktor Orban of overseeing a surge in last-minute spending that risks overshooting deficit targets this year.
title: Magyar Warns Orban’s Last-Minute Spree Endangers Hungary Budget

author: Jorge Valero
description: The International Monetary Fund argued the European Union should delay billions in repayments for Covid-era debt to help free up money for defense or infrastructure spending.
title: IMF Backs Macron’s Call for Rolling Over EU’s Covid Debt

author: Erica Yokoyama, James Mayger
description: Relations with China have been tense since Sanae Takaichi commented on Taiwan.
title: Japan’s Diplomatic Offensive Has One Major Gap

author: Marton Kasnyik, Thomas Escritt
description: One of Hungary’s most powerful media executives offered to hand his business to the state for free, the latest sign of the shift among some of the country’s richest following Viktor Orban‘s landslide election defeat.
title: Orban Ally Offers to Hand Media Empire to Hungary After Election

author: Jacob Reid
description: Prime Minister Keir Starmer warned Iran against encouraging antisemitism in Britain, saying UK authorities are investigating whether a foreign state was behind some of the recent attacks on the country’s Jewish community.
title: Starmer Warns Iran Against Encouraging Hatred Towards British Jews

author: Simon Marks, Fasika Tadesse
description: Sudan and Ethiopia traded accusations after a drone attack on the war-torn nation’s capital, Khartoum, that’s ratcheted up tensions between the African neighbors.
title: Sudan and Ethiopia Trade Barbs After Drone Attack on Khartoum

author: Leen Al-Rashdan
description: The United Arab Emirates has partially closed its airspace for the first time in several weeks after Iran launched missiles and drones toward the UAE, in the worst flareup since the ceasefire began less than a month ago.
title: UAE Restricts Airspace for Jets After Iran Launched Missiles

author: Andreina Itriago, Fabiola Zerpa
description: Since President Nicolás Maduro was captured by US forces and ousted from office on Jan. 3, Venezuela has entered a fast-changing and uncertain phase shaped heavily by Washington. Relations between the US and Venezuela have shifted from isolation to direct engagement: The Trump administration has restored diplomatic ties and is working with interim President Delcy Rodríguez. But that relationship is highly conditional. The US is using sanctions relief, access to global finance and control over oi
title: Welcome to the New Venezuela: How the US Is Reshaping Its Old Foe

author: Helen Nyambura
description: Tanzanian President Samia Suluhu Hassan said she wasn’t consulted over a plan to establish a 650,000 barrels-a-day refinery in her nation, with the plant jointly owned by East African countries and Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote.
title: Tanzanian Leader Rebukes Kenya’s Ruto Over Planned Refinery

author: Sanne Wass
description: Negotiations to form Denmark’s government are set to become the longest in the Nordic country’s history as caretaker Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen continues to lead the political bargaining process six weeks after the election.
title: Danish Coalition Talks Near Record as Frederiksen Seeks Deal

author: Eltaf Najafizada, Omar Tamo
description: The fragile US-Iran ceasefire held Tuesday morning after a day of clashes involving shipping in the Strait of Hormuz and missile attacks against the United Arab Emirates.
title: US-Iran Ceasefire Holds After Hormuz Clashes and UAE Strikes

description: The US and Iran exchanged fire in a flareup of violence on Monday that also drew in the United Arab Emirates, prompting calls for renewed strikes on Iranian targets and casting doubt on the fate of a four-week ceasefire. Bloomberg's Joumanna Bercetche has the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Hormuz Fighting Raises Prospect of Fresh US Strikes on Iran

author: Anuchit Nguyen
description: Thailand’s government plans to raise 400 billion baht ($12 billion) in new debt to support farmers, low-income households, and small businesses affected by the fallout from the Middle East conflict, while accelerating the country’s shift away from fossil fuels.
title: Thailand Eyes $12 Billion in New Debt to Cushion Mideast Crisis

author: Shruti Srivastava, Sudhi Ranjan Sen
description: India’s opposition parties allege large-scale violations in counting of votes that led to Bharatiya Janata Party’s landslide victory in West Bengal, ousting Mamata Banerjee’s Trinamool Congress.
title: Modi Opponents Allege Vote Count Violations After Key State Loss

author: Alaric Nightingale
description: Russia’s Kirishi oil refinery near the Baltic coast is on fire after overnight drone strikes, according to NASA satellite images, as Ukraine ramps up attacks ahead of planned Victory Day ceasefires.
title: Russia’s Kirishi Oil Refinery on Fire, NASA Satellites Show

author: Ruchi Bhatia
description: Implementing populist promises that featured prominently in election wins in key Indian states this week risk straining their finances, with economists warning of wider fiscal deficits.
title: Election Pledges in India Risk Wider Deficits, Economists Warn

description:
India’s ruling BJP has strengthened Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s political position after decisive state election victories, reshaping the balance between government and opposition. Rahul Verma, Fellow at the Centre for Policy Research and Associate Professor at Shiv Nadar University, spoke on Insight with Haslinda Amin about the implications for governance, reforms, and India’s North-South divide.
Kurien Abraham (Source: Bloomberg)
title: BJP's State Poll Wins Strengthen Modi's Grip on India

author: Anthony Halpin
description: Ukrainian drones are regularly hitting targets deep inside Russia, reaching to the Ural Mountains and communities where most people had seen the war as a distant problem.
title: Ukraine’s Long-Range Drones Now Strike 1,000 Miles Inside Russia

description: President Donald Trump said he's looking forward to meeting Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, signaling that his plans for the high-stakes summit are still on despite fresh tensions between the world's two largest economies. Bloomberg's Minmin Low reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: Trump-Xi Meeting Approaches Even as Tensions Mount

author: Laura Avetisyan, Rose Henderson
description: Polls show the SNP is on course to win a fifth straight term in this week’s election after Labour’s collapse in popularity.
title: Starmer’s Troubles Breathe New Life Into Scotland’s Nationalists

author: Nectar Gan
description: US President Donald Trump said he will raise the case of Hong Kong’s imprisoned former media tycoon Jimmy Lai in his upcoming summit with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, adding a potential friction point to an agenda already complicated by the Iran war.
title: Trump Says He Will Bring Up Hong Kong’s Jimmy Lai in Xi Summit

author: Rajesh Roy, Sudhi Ranjan Sen, Sanjai P R
description: In most of his films, Tamil superstar C. Joseph Vijay has saved the nation and its poor from powerful forces. He used that same script in politics this week to emerge as the unlikely winner in elections in one of India’s most economically important states.
title: India’s iPhone Hub Stunned by Movie Star Vijay’s Political Rise

author: Andra Timu, Irina Vilcu
description: Romanian lawmakers will vote on ousting Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan in a move that could plunge the country into a renewed political crisis and imperil efforts to narrow the widest budget deficit in the European Union.
title: Romania Prepares to Oust Premier Without Plan for the Day After

author: Yian Lee
description: President Lai Ching-te said Taiwan’s leaders have the right to engage with the world and visit the leaders of allied countries, after returning from an African mission that his administration claims was nearly thwarted by China.
title: Taiwan’s Lai Insists On Right to Visit Allies After Africa Trip

author: Derek Wallbank
description: A top Senate Republican has proposed spending as much as $1 billion for US Secret Service security adjustments and upgrades, including for President Donald Trump’s planned White House ballroom.
title: Senate GOP Seeks $1 Billion for Secret Service, Trump Ballroom

author: Stephen Wicary
description: A Canadian mining company that is among Cuba’s largest foreign investors is consulting with advisers and stakeholders after President Donald Trump expanded US sanctions against the struggling Caribbean nation.
title: Canadian Miner Invested in Cuba Says It's Assessing Trump's Fresh Sanctions

author: Myles Miller
description: A man was shot by Secret Service officers near the White House Monday afternoon after agents spotted him carrying a concealed firearm and he opened fire, according to the agency’s deputy director.
title: Secret Service Officers Shoot Gunman Near the White House

description: The US and Iran exchanged fire in the Persian Gulf in a flareup of violence on Monday that also drew in the United Arab Emirates, prompting calls for renewed strikes on Iranian targets and casting doubt on the fate of a four-week ceasefire. Bloomberg's Derek Wallbank breaks down the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)
title: US and Iran Trade Fire, Jolting Four-Week-Old Ceasefire
